answer: Each identity banks one relic yarrow lot in the seed atlas: it locks 70 credits, files one accession for its lot, with weight and sprout count. An auditor germinates a sample and recounts sprouts; a shortfall, reused accession, or a second claim burns the bond. First accession costs 31, the kth 31+6(k-1), the 1000th 6025; 1000 false identities pay 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked, each needing a lot. A rented-seed ring fails because the atlas rejects duplicate accessions and one sample cannot match two filings. An honest banker pays 31 once and recovers the bond after a clean count.
